name: Client identity, approval, clock and cart operation mirrors

comparisons.reasoning: Five approval helpers same bool short-circuit, min4inputlength, one server IssueManagerApproval call and returned issued token/approver IDs. No client-selected arbitrary authority accepted from successful result.
comparisons.callers_context: Cashier Operations345, ControlCenter136, Employees390, Inventory696,Purchasing604 bodies read; actual call sites pass operation-specific permission/reason and UI error callback.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: needsApproval is client UX only; false returns no token and server must still authorize. No live PIN values inspected or credentials saved. Different submitted action values, retry persistence and command writers remain outside helper.
comparisons.recommendation: Share a typed approval-prompt service preserving server authority, error callback and action-specific permission; never auto-send second issuing call for local validation.

comparisons.reasoning: Three login Submit bodies identical: busy/error, API LoginByPin, failure clears input, success assigns CurrentUser then clears and emits LoggedIn, exception shows message, finally clears busy.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter/legacyWPF/CashierWinUI exact bodies, CanSubmit guards length>=4,!IsBusy and Toolkit relay generation read. Prior API transport comparison retained.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Same code does not prove same API type/session role acceptance. Token/session change can occur in API before subsequent shell role check (prior UI020), not a new mirrored finding. No authentication automated or account tested.
comparisons.recommendation: Common login orchestration with UI-framework facade, preserve role/session acceptance and bearer-clear on rejected role; no fix applied.
tests: Same current user and bearer state

comparisons.reasoning: Three UpdateClock methods use DateTime.Now and ar-EG clock/day formatting, independent server Cairo BusinessClock. Identical output logic.
comparisons.callers_context: Headers timer Tick and constructor UpdateClock call, WinUI versus WPF framework types differ.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Workstation timezone display can differ backend restaurant date; same source body not a durable business-day policy. No malicious timer inferred from visible clock update.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared pure date formatting with explicit clock/zone input while keeping platform timer adapters.

comparisons.reasoning: Two WinUI Header.Refresh methods notify same6computed properties, no fetch or mutation. Captured AppSession differs by client capability.
comparisons.callers_context: Header getters and Cashier ctor OperationStateChanged subscription; CallCenter explicit Refresh callers versus main session lifecycle separate.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Notification equality does not mean all triggering events subscribed equally. No permission enforced by visibility update.
comparisons.recommendation: Share computed-header notification helper only with explicit lifecycle/subscription policy.
tests: No stale badge after session switch

comparisons.reasoning: CallCenterWinUI and legacyWPF constructors same session assignment, initial clock update,30sDispatcherTimer tick/start. DispatcherTimer symbols bind different UI frameworks. CashierWinUI near-copy adds OperationStateChanged subscription.
comparisons.callers_context: Full Header ctor context and CashierWinUI20-29 Stop method read; main shell Stop calls Header.Stop.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Intentional platform adapters; timer only clock text, not financial posting. No actual leak proven merely live timer. Merging bodies across platform assemblies not directly drop-in.
comparisons.recommendation: Common clock presentation logic with platform-owned timer/dispose adapters and explicit unsubscribe lifecycle.
tests: No multiple timer after repeated screen creation

comparisons.reasoning: Three AppSession.HasPermission bodies check nonnull CurrentUser and exact permission/all membership. They do not check Active, refresh/revoke token or validate issued server role.
comparisons.callers_context: Actual session code and counterpart declarations read; Cashier session draft/management unresolved-operation state differs CallCenter/legacy.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Advisory client command availability only, server Actor policy includes active identity. Do not claim missing Active check automatically bypasses actual server authorization.
comparisons.recommendation: Share permission-view helper using common user contract, retain server as authority and per-client operation lifecycle state.

comparisons.reasoning: AppendNoteText same CanEditOperation guard and comma-separated appended line Notes. Captured CartLine and root operation predicates belong separate clients.
comparisons.callers_context: Cashier/CallCenter bodies and State CanEditOperation definitions read; cart-note UI routes call this direct helper.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Cashier guard includes many retained financial operations, CallCenter includes checkout/print. Same body correct abstraction only with caller operation policy; note mutation not financial authorization.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared line-note formatting/command helper parameterized edit eligibility; keep notes in server CheckoutItem request.

comparisons.reasoning: Three checkout item selectors serialize ProductId/VariantId/Quantity/AppliedOfferId/Notes into same shared Application CheckoutItemRequest. No client unit price included.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenterCheckout142, legacy102,CashierWinUI353; surrounding requests differ split method and DiscountPiastres0versusactive discount.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Intentional shared line contract, server revalidates effective offer/product amounts. Identical selector does not make complete order payment/tax/discount payload equal.
comparisons.recommendation: One mapper for cart-line contract preserving station-specific checkout envelope.

comparisons.reasoning: Two DecreaseQuantity handlers guard CanEditOperation, decrement above1 else remove, then recompute local totals. Different parent subtotal/tax/comp capability intentionally remains.
comparisons.callers_context: Cashier/CallCenter bodies, parent RecomputeCartTotals and state predicates read; Cashier NotifyTotals extra notifications.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: UI estimates not authoritative server totals; subtotal-sum same, Cashier subtracts discount/tax+fee-comp while CallCenter plain tax+delivery (no comp/discount). Domain CheckoutRules93-97 agrees shared order of operations for supported inputs; not all client feature parity.
comparisons.recommendation: Share cart-line mutation while keeping specialized financial estimate policy and server authority.

comparisons.reasoning: Three digit-entry handlers guard EXISTING Pin.Length>=6, then append provided digit string and clear error. Does not validate parameter is one digit; normal keypad binding constrains it.
comparisons.callers_context: Login CanSubmit length>=4,!busy plus command declarations; WPF and WinUI wrappers share rule.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Multi-character programmatic parameter can exceed6; no server PIN bypass inferred from UI parameter contract. No actual PIN literal or login operation used.
comparisons.recommendation: Share input normalization with explicit one-digit contract if desired; preserve server independent validation.

comparisons.reasoning: Three OnIsBusyChanged hooks notify CanEditAction and register !CanEditAction in shared session. Captured predicates differ Delivery(assign/outcome/settle),Inventory(count/waste),Purchasing(supplier/receive/pay).
comparisons.callers_context: Actual predicate lines before each hook and AppSession.SetManagementOperationPending identity-set implementation read.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Shared busy callback is global close/lock coordination, not only animation. Pending request transitions must also refresh registration even without busy change; no complete lifecycle correctness inferred.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared operation-state adapter parameterized actual pending predicate, preserve register/unregister owner lifetime.
tests: No lock/close while financial outcome unknown

comparisons.reasoning: Two selected-category hooks refresh catalogue then mark tile selected by object ReferenceEquals, not ID string. Same instance assumption in each client.
comparisons.callers_context: RefreshVisibleProducts bodies route current category or search-across-categories with icon-by-product lookup, read bounded context.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Reload producing new DTO instances must rebuild selection references, else highlight can differ; not a proven runtime defect. No financial product validation via tile identity.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared catalogue presentation state with explicit selected identity policy and separate station actions.

comparisons.reasoning: Two health checks await PingHealth then update IsOnline only if not stopped. Full root shells use5sDispatcherTimer and initial fire-and-forget check; Cashier adds recovered-operation notice.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter constructor/Stop37-54 and Cashier constructor/CheckHealth contexts read.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: No serialization/cancellation token here, so overlapping pings can complete out of order if duration>interval; indicator is endpoint availability, not proven database/financial readiness. No live ping executed.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared cancellable/singleflight health observer with UI adapters; keep unrelated operation-close guards distinct.
tests: Endpoint healthy but DB failure separately

comparisons.reasoning: Two RemoveLine handlers guard CanEditOperation then remove item and recompute totals. Same mutation body, separate CartLine classes and specialized pending-operation guards.
comparisons.callers_context: Cashier274-275/CallCenter289-290 plus RecomputeCartTotals and State definitions inspected.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Cannot remove line while unresolved checkout per UI predicate; server retains final request authority. No financial write in these handlers.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared cart command behavior if preserving station estimate and edit-state policy.
